question.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=96$ from a population where $72%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that more than $70%$ but less than $80%$ of the sample has the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size. *Hint: Two tables of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.04\,$$\,0.05\,$$\,0.06\,$
$\,1.7\,$ $\,0.9591\,$ $\,0.9599\,$ $\,0.9608\,$
$\,1.8\,$ $\,0.9671\,$ $\,0.9678\,$ $\,0.9686\,$
$\,1.9\,$ $\,0.9738\,$ $\,0.9744\,$ $\,0.9750\,$
$z$$\,0.04\,$$\,0.05\,$$\,0.06\,$
$\,-0.4\,$ $\,0.3300\,$ $\,0.3264\,$ $\,0.3228\,$
$\,-0.3\,$ $\,0.3669\,$ $\,0.3632\,$ $\,0.3594\,$
$\,-0.2\,$ $\,0.4052\,$ $\,0.4013\,$ $\,0.3974\,$
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=96,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.72.$

Now, since

$$
np=96(0.72)=69.12>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=96(1-0.72)=26.88>5,
$$

and $n=96$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.72,\frac{0.72(1-0.72)}{96}) \\  & ∼N(0.72,0.0021).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(0.7<\overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.8).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.7<\overset{^}{\,p}<0.8) & =P(\frac{0.7-0.72}{\sqrt{0.0021}}<Z\le \frac{0.8-0.72}{\sqrt{0.0021}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.44<Z\le 1.75) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.75)-P(Z\le -0.44) \\  & =Φ(1.75)-Φ(-0.44)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.75) & =0.9599 \\ Φ(-0.44) & =0.3300.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.7<\overset{^}{\,p}<0.8) & =Φ(1.75)-Φ(-0.44) \\  & =0.9599-0.3300 \\  & =0.6299.\end{aligned}
$$
